title: The pretérito perfeito
description: Say what you did: regular endings, spelling changes in the eu form and the common irregular verbs.

guide.summary: The pretérito perfeito is the everyday past tense for finished actions: I spoke, she ate, we went. This page has the endings for the three families, the spelling changes in the eu form, and the irregular verbs you will use most, plus the time words that go with them.

sections.title: Regular -ar verbs
sections.text: Remove -ar from the infinitive and add the past ending for your subject. Você, ele and ela share one form, and so do vocês, eles and elas.
steps: Find the subject: who did it?
Remove -ar from the infinitive to get the stem.
Add the ending on that subject’s row.

examples.pt: Ontem eu falei com a minha mãe.
examples.en: Yesterday I spoke with my mother.

watch: Eu ends in -ei and ele in -ou: do not swap them.
The pretérito perfeito is for finished actions. What you used to do goes in the imperfeito.

sections.title: Regular -er and -ir verbs
sections.text: The -er and -ir families share the eu and nós pattern: a vowel plus -i or -mos. The vowel of the family, e or i, shows in every form.
steps: Check the infinitive: -er or -ir?
Remove the ending to get the stem.
Use e for -er verbs and i for -ir verbs, then the ending for the subject.
watch: Never give an -er verb the -ou of -ar verbs: bebeu, not bebou.
Like -ar verbs, the nós form of -er and -ir verbs looks the same as the present: comemos, abrimos.

sections.title: Nós falamos: present or past?
sections.text: For -ar verbs the nós past is spelled exactly like the nós present. Time words tell you which one is meant, and they are worth learning with the tense.
steps: Write nós with -amos, as in the present.
Look at the time words around the verb: ontem, passado, passada and já point to the past.
Do not change the spelling of the verb to show the past.

examples.pt: Ontem nós falamos com o professor.
examples.en: Yesterday we spoke with the teacher.

watch: Falemos and compremos are subjunctive forms, not past ones.
In Portugal the past is written falámos, but in Brazil there is no accent.
A gente takes the ele form: a gente falou.

sections.title: Spelling changes in the eu form
sections.text: The eu ending -ei starts with e, which would change the sound of c, g and ç. The spelling changes so the verb keeps the sound of its infinitive. Only the eu form is affected.
steps: Check the infinitive: does it end in -car, -gar or -çar?
-car: write -quei. -gar: write -guei.
-çar: drop the cedilla and write -cei.
Every other person keeps the normal spelling.
watch: Portuguese never writes çe or çi: the cedilla is only for a, o and u.
Nós is not affected: nós pagamos, nós jogamos.

sections.title: Ser and ir: one past for two verbs
sections.text: Ser, to be, and ir, to go, have exactly the same past forms. The rest of the sentence tells you which is meant: a place with a or para means went.
steps: Find the subject.
Take the form on its row: fui, foi, fomos or foram.
Read on: a place after the verb means went, a description means was.
watch: Fui is eu and foi is ele: one letter apart.
Vamos and vai are present forms of ir, not past ones.

sections.title: Ter, estar, fazer, poder, querer, dizer
sections.text: These common verbs change their stem in the past. The eu form ends in -e or has no ending, and the ele form often differs from it only by one vowel.
steps: Recognise the verb: it is one of the six on this list.
Pick the form on the row for your subject.
For poder with ele or ela, write the circumflex: pôde.
watch: Pode without the circumflex is the present; pôde is the past.
Quis and disse are spelled with s, never z or c.
Never add regular endings: fazeu, dizeu and podeu do not exist.

sections.title: Ver and dar
sections.text: Ver has very short past forms. Dar ends in -ar, but in the past it takes endings like an -er verb.
steps: Ver: vi, viu, vimos, viram.
Dar: dei, deu, demos, deram.
Do not use the regular -ar endings for dar.
watch: Dar has no -ou and no -aram: deu and deram.
Vejo and vê are present forms of ver.

steps: Find the subject, then remove -ar from the infinitive.
Add the past ending on that subject’s row: -ei, -ou, -amos or -aram.
Check you have not written a present ending such as -o or -a.
Check whether the verb ends in -er or -ir.
Keep the vowel of the family: -i, -eu, -emos, -eram or -i, -iu, -imos, -iram.
Never use the -ou of -ar verbs.
Write nós with -amos, exactly as in the present.
Let the time word, such as ontem or semana passada, show the past.
Check the infinitive ending: -car, -gar or -çar.
In the eu form write -quei, -guei or -cei.
Keep the normal spelling for every other person.
Remember that ser and ir share one past.
Pick fui, foi, fomos or foram for the subject.
Recognise the irregular verb.
Take the form for the subject from the table.
Watch the circumflex in pôde and the s in quis and disse.
Ver: vi, viu, vimos, viram.
Dar: dei, deu, demos, deram, never the regular -ar endings.

mistakes.why: Falou is the form for você, ele and ela. Eu has its own ending in the past.
Falo is the present: I speak. The question asks for a finished action in the past.
Falamos is the nós form, we. The subject here is one person, the speaker.

exercises.hint: Start from the stem fal-. Which ending goes with eu in the past?
exercises.feedback: Eu forms of -ar verbs end in -ei.
exercises.explanation: Eu falei: fal- + -ei.

exercises.instruction: Write trabalhar in the pretérito perfeito.

mistakes.why: Trabalhei is the eu form. The subject of this sentence is she.
Trabalha is the present. Ontem places the action in the past, so the verb must be a past form.
Trabalharam is the plural form, for eles, elas and vocês. Ela is one person.

exercises.hint: Ela takes the same ending as você and ele.
exercises.feedback: Você, ele and ela forms of -ar verbs end in -ou.
exercises.explanation: Ela trabalhou: trabalh- + -ou.

mistakes.why: Comprou is the form for one person: você, ele or ela. Eles is several people.
Compramos is the nós form, a group that includes the speaker. Eles are people being talked about.
Comprei is the eu form, the speaker alone.

exercises.hint: Look for the plural past ending.
exercises.feedback: Eles forms of -ar verbs end in -aram.
exercises.explanation: Eles compraram: compr- + -aram. They bought the car on Saturday.

mistakes.why: Estudou is the form for você, ele and ela. With eu the verb takes its own ending.

exercises.hint: The eu ending of -ar verbs in the past is -ei.
exercises.feedback: One verb tile has the ele ending.
exercises.explanation: Eu estudei: estud- + -ei.

exercises.source: You (plural) worked a lot last week.
answers: Vocês trabalharam muito na semana passada.
Vocês trabalhou muito na semana passada.
mistakes.why: Trabalhou is the singular form, for one person. Vocês is plural.

answers: Vocês trabalham muito na semana passada.
mistakes.why: Trabalham is the present. Last week asks for a past form.

answers: Vocês trabalharão muito na semana passada.
mistakes.why: Trabalharão is the future, which cannot go with last week.

exercises.hint: Vocês takes the same past ending as eles.
exercises.feedback: Use the plural past form of trabalhar.
exercises.explanation: Vocês trabalharam: trabalh- + -aram. Semana passada works with or without na in front.

exercises.instruction: Put the sentence in the pretérito perfeito.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged, still in the present.
Comprou is the form for você, ele and ela, not for eu.
Comprava is the imperfeito, for what you used to do. Here the action is a single finished one.

exercises.hint: Swap the present ending -o for the past eu ending.
exercises.feedback: The eu past of -ar verbs ends in -ei.
exercises.explanation: Eu comprei pão: compr- + -ei. I bought bread.

mistakes.why: Comeu is the form for one person: você, ele or ela.
Comem is the present: they eat. The question asks for the past.
The ending -aram belongs to -ar verbs. Comer is an -er verb and keeps its e.

exercises.hint: Stem com-, then the plural past ending for -er verbs.
exercises.feedback: Eles forms of -er verbs end in -eram.
exercises.explanation: Eles comeram: com- + -eram.

exercises.instruction: Write abrir in the pretérito perfeito.

mistakes.why: Abri is the eu form. The question is about you.
Abre is the present. Asking whether it was done needs the past.
Abrir is an -ir verb: its ending is -iu, not the -ou of -ar verbs, and it goes on the stem abr-.

exercises.hint: Você takes the same ending as ele.
exercises.feedback: Você forms of -ir verbs end in -iu.
exercises.explanation: Você abriu: abr- + -iu. Did you open the window?

mistakes.why: Escreveu is the form for você, ele and ela, not for the speaker.
The ending -ei belongs to -ar verbs. Escrever is an -er verb, so eu takes a different ending.
Escrevo is the present. Ontem needs a past form.

exercises.hint: Escrever is an -er verb. What is its eu ending in the past?
exercises.feedback: The eu past of -er verbs ends in -i.
exercises.explanation: Eu escrevi: escrev- + -i. I wrote the letter yesterday.

mistakes.why: The ending -ou belongs to -ar verbs. Beber is an -er verb.
Bebi is the eu form. The subject is she.
Bebe is the present: she drinks. The English is in the past.

exercises.hint: Beber is an -er verb. Ela takes -eu.
exercises.feedback: Ela forms of -er verbs end in -eu.
exercises.explanation: Ela bebeu: beb- + -eu.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. Dormiu is the form for one person.
The ending -eram belongs to -er verbs. Dormir is an -ir verb.
Dormem is the present. The sentence was in the past and should stay there.

exercises.hint: Dormiu is singular. Eles is plural.
exercises.feedback: Eles needs the plural past ending.
exercises.explanation: Eles dormiram: dorm- + -iram. They slept well.

exercises.instruction: Put the sentence in the pretérito perfeito.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged, still in the present.
The ending -ou is for -ar verbs. Vender keeps the e of its family.
The ending -iu is for -ir verbs. Vender is an -er verb.

exercises.hint: Vender is an -er verb. Which past ending goes with ela?
exercises.feedback: Ela forms of -er verbs end in -eu.
exercises.explanation: Ela vendeu: vend- + -eu. She sold the car.

mistakes.why: Falemos is the subjunctive, used in phrases like let us speak. It is not a past form.
Falaram is the form for eles, elas and vocês. Nós includes the speaker.
Falou is the form for one person: você, ele or ela.

exercises.hint: For -ar verbs the nós past looks exactly like the nós present.
exercises.feedback: Nós falamos is both present and past. Ontem tells you it is past.
exercises.explanation: Nós falamos: fal- + -amos. Yesterday we spoke with the teacher.

mistakes.why: Jogaram is the form for eles, elas and vocês, people other than the speaker.
Joguei is the eu form. The gu spelling only appears there.
Jogou is the form for one person: você, ele or ela.

exercises.hint: Nós ends in -amos, in the past as in the present.
exercises.feedback: The nós past of -ar verbs ends in -amos. Domingo passado makes it past.
exercises.explanation: Nós jogamos: jog- + -amos. We played football last Sunday.

exercises.instruction: Write viajar in the pretérito perfeito.
exercises.source: Na semana passada nós ____ (viajar) para a praia.

mistakes.why: Viajaram is the form for eles, elas and vocês. Nós includes the speaker.
Viajou is the form for one person: você, ele or ela.
Viajemos is the subjunctive, not a past form.

exercises.hint: Nós takes the same ending as in the present.
exercises.feedback: The nós past of -ar verbs ends in -amos.
exercises.explanation: Nós viajamos: viaj- + -amos. Last week we went to the beach.

mistakes.why: Compraram is the form for eles and vocês, not for nós.
Comprou is the form for one person: você, ele or ela.
Compremos is the subjunctive, not a past form.

exercises.hint: The nós past looks like the present. Ontem does the work.
exercises.feedback: Use compramos, the nós past of comprar.
exercises.explanation: Nós compramos: compr- + -amos. Ontem can go first or last.

mistakes.why: Pagaram is the form for eles, elas and vocês. Nós needs its own ending.

exercises.hint: Já means already and goes before the verb.
exercises.feedback: One verb tile is the eles form.
exercises.explanation: Nós já pagamos: pag- + -amos. Only the eu form of pagar adds a u.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. Estudaram is the form for eles, elas and vocês.
Estudou is the form for one person: você, ele or ela.
Estudemos is the subjunctive, not a past form.

exercises.hint: Estudaram belongs to eles.
exercises.feedback: Nós takes -amos in the past too.
exercises.explanation: Nós estudamos: estud- + -amos. Ontem shows it is past.

mistakes.why: Without the u, ge would be read like the s in measure. The verb has to keep the hard sound of chegar.
Chegou is the form for você, ele and ela, not for eu.
Chego is the present: I arrive.

exercises.hint: Before -ei, g would sound like the s in measure. How do you keep it hard?
exercises.feedback: Verbs in -gar write -guei in the eu form.
exercises.explanation: Eu cheguei: g becomes gu before e to keep the hard g of chegar.

exercises.instruction: Write ficar in the pretérito perfeito.

mistakes.why: Ce is read like se, so ficei would not sound like ficar. The k sound needs another spelling before e.
Ficou is the form for você, ele and ela, not for eu.
Fico is the present: I stay.

exercises.hint: Before -ei, a c would sound like s. Which spelling keeps the k sound?
exercises.feedback: Verbs in -car write -quei in the eu form.
exercises.explanation: Eu fiquei: c becomes qu before e. I stayed at home on Saturday.

mistakes.why: The cedilla is only needed before a, o and u. Before e a plain c already has the s sound, so Portuguese never writes çe.
Começou is the form for você, ele and ela, not for eu.
Começo is the present: I start.

exercises.hint: Before e, a plain c already sounds like s.
exercises.feedback: Verbs in -çar drop the cedilla in the eu form: -cei.
exercises.explanation: Eu comecei: ç becomes c before e. I started the class early.

exercises.instruction: Fix the spelling of the verb.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. Ge does not sound like the g of pagar.
Pagou is the form for você, ele and ela, not for eu.
Writing j changes the sound completely. Pagar keeps a hard g in every form.

exercises.hint: Ge sounds like the s in measure. Pagar has a hard g.
exercises.feedback: Verbs in -gar write -guei in the eu form.
exercises.explanation: Eu paguei: the u keeps the g hard. I paid the bill.

mistakes.why: Without the u, ge would be read like the s in measure. Jogar keeps its hard g.
Jogou is the form for você, ele and ela, not for eu.
Jogo is the present: I play. The English is in the past.

exercises.hint: Jogar ends in -gar. Watch the eu spelling.
exercises.feedback: Eu joguei: g becomes gu before e.
exercises.explanation: Eu joguei futebol: the u keeps the hard g of jogar.

exercises.instruction: Change ele to eu and adjust the verb.

mistakes.why: The cedilla is only needed before a, o and u. Before e a plain c already sounds like s.
Almoçou is the form for ele, the subject you were asked to replace.

exercises.hint: The eu ending starts with e. What happens to the cedilla?
exercises.feedback: Almoçar writes almocei: no cedilla before e.
exercises.explanation: Eu almocei: ç becomes c before e. I had lunch early.

mistakes.why: Vamos is the present: we go, or let us go.
Foram is the form for eles, elas and vocês.
Ir is irregular and does not take the regular -ir endings.

exercises.hint: Ir shares its past with ser.
exercises.feedback: The nós past of ir and ser is fomos.
exercises.explanation: Nós fomos: the same word means we went and we were.

mistakes.why: Foi is the form for one person: você, ele or ela.
Fomos is the nós form, a group that includes the speaker.
Ir is irregular. Its past is built on fo-, not on the infinitive.

exercises.hint: Ao cinema tells you this is ir, to go. Look for the eles form.
exercises.feedback: The eles past of ir is foram.
exercises.explanation: Eles foram ao cinema: they went to the cinema yesterday.

exercises.instruction: Write ser in the pretérito perfeito.

mistakes.why: Fui is the eu form. The subject is the party.
Foram is the plural form. A festa is one thing.
É is the present: the party is great. The sentence talks about a party that is over.
Era is the imperfeito, for describing how things used to be or were going on. The party is over and the task asks for the pretérito perfeito.

exercises.hint: A festa counts as ela. Ser and ir share this form.
exercises.feedback: The ela past of ser is foi.
exercises.explanation: A festa foi ótima: the party was great. It is over, so it takes the pretérito perfeito.

mistakes.why: Foi is the form for você, ele and ela, not for eu.

exercises.hint: Ir is irregular. The eu form is short.
exercises.feedback: One verb tile is the ele form.
exercises.explanation: Eu fui ao mercado: fui is the eu past of ir and ser.

Onde você foi no fim de semana passado?

mistakes.why: Fui is the eu form. The question asks about you.

answers: Aonde você vai no fim de semana passado?
mistakes.why: Vai is the present. Last weekend asks for the past.

exercises.hint: Você takes the same past form as ele.
exercises.feedback: The você past of ir is foi.
exercises.explanation: Aonde você foi: foi is the past of ir for você. Onde is also common in speech.

exercises.instruction: Put the sentence in the pretérito perfeito.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged, still in the present.
Foram is the form for eles, elas and vocês.
Íamos is the imperfeito, for what you used to do. Here it is one finished trip.

exercises.hint: Vamos is the present of ir.
exercises.feedback: The nós past of ir is fomos.
exercises.explanation: Nós fomos à praia: we went to the beach.

mistakes.why: Fazer is irregular: it does not take the regular -er endings.
Fez is the form for você, ele and ela, not for eu.
Faço is the present: I do.

exercises.hint: Fazer changes its stem in the past. The eu form has three letters.
exercises.feedback: The eu past of fazer is fiz.
exercises.explanation: Eu fiz: an irregular form to learn by heart.

mistakes.why: Without the circumflex this is the present: she can. The mark is the only thing that makes it past.
Pude is the eu form. Ela takes a different vowel.
Poder is irregular: it does not take the regular -er endings.

exercises.hint: The past form looks like the present but carries a mark.
exercises.feedback: The ela past of poder is pôde, with a circumflex.
exercises.explanation: Ela pôde: the circumflex is what separates she could from the present she can.

mistakes.why: Teve is the form for você, ele and ela, not for eu.
Tenho is the present. Ontem needs a past form.
Ter is irregular: it does not take the regular -er endings.

exercises.hint: Ter is irregular. The eu form ends in -e.
exercises.feedback: The eu past of ter is tive.
exercises.explanation: Eu tive muito trabalho: I had a lot of work yesterday.

exercises.instruction: Write querer in the pretérito perfeito.

mistakes.why: Quer is the present: she does not want.
The sound is right, but this form is spelled with s at the end.
Querer is irregular: it does not take the regular -er endings.

exercises.hint: Querer has a short irregular past, the same for eu and ela.
exercises.feedback: The ela past of querer is quis.
exercises.explanation: Ela não quis sair: she did not want to go out, or she refused to go out.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. Dizer does not take the regular -er endings.
Dice is not a Portuguese form. The s sound in the past of dizer is written with ss.
Diz is the present: he tells the truth. The sentence was in the past.

exercises.hint: Dizer is irregular. Its past has a double s.
exercises.feedback: The ele past of dizer is disse.
exercises.explanation: Ele disse a verdade: he told the truth.

mistakes.why: Fazer is irregular: it does not take the regular -er endings.
Fiz is the eu form. The question asks about you.
Faz is the present. Ontem needs a past form.

exercises.hint: Você takes the ele form. Fazer is irregular.
exercises.feedback: The você past of fazer is fez.
exercises.explanation: O que você fez ontem: fez is the past of fazer for você.

exercises.source: I was at Maria’s house yesterday.
answers: Eu estive na casa da Maria ontem.
Eu esteve na casa da Maria ontem.
mistakes.why: Esteve is the form for você, ele and ela, not for eu.

exercises.hint: Estar is irregular. The eu form ends in -e.
exercises.feedback: One verb tile is the ele form.
exercises.explanation: Eu estive: the eu past of estar, for a visit that is over.

mistakes.why: Vejo is the present: I see.
Viu is the form for você, ele and ela, not for eu.
The ending -ei belongs to -ar verbs. Ver works like an -er verb here.

exercises.hint: Ver has a very short past. The eu form has two letters.
exercises.feedback: The eu past of ver is vi.
exercises.explanation: Eu vi: I saw.

mistakes.why: Vi is the eu form. The question asks about you.
Viram is the form for eles, elas and vocês. Você is one person.
Ver is irregular here: its past takes an i, not the -eu of regular -er verbs.

exercises.hint: Você takes the same past form as ele.
exercises.feedback: The você past of ver is viu.
exercises.explanation: Você viu o filme ontem: did you see the film yesterday?

exercises.instruction: Write dar in the pretérito perfeito.

mistakes.why: Dou is the present, and only for eu.
Dei is the eu form. The subject is my father.
Dar is irregular: its past does not take the regular -ou of -ar verbs.

exercises.hint: Dar ends in -ar but takes -er style endings in the past.
exercises.feedback: The ele past of dar is deu.
exercises.explanation: Meu pai me deu um presente: my father gave me a gift.

exercises.source: We saw Maria at the party.
answers: Nós vimos a Maria na festa.
Nós viu a Maria na festa.

answers: Nós vemos a Maria na festa.

answers: Nós viram a Maria na festa.
mistakes.why: Viram is the form for eles, elas and vocês.

exercises.hint: The nós past of ver ends in -imos.
